summary: Construction, improvement and repair of real property is not taxed to the owner in Maine; the contractor pays tax on materials as their last user.

citations.title: MRS Instructional Bulletin No. 4, Contractors and Subcontractors (last revised July 22, 2024)
citations.quote: The term “construction contract,” as used in this bulletin, means a contract for repair, alteration, improvement, remodeling or construction of real property.

citations.title: MRS Instructional Bulletin No. 4, Contractors and Subcontractors (last revised July 22, 2024)
citations.quote: The contractor, as the last user of the materials as tangible personal property, pays a sales or use tax when purchasing the materials.

notes: A contractor that registers as a retailer and passes title to materials before incorporation (e.g. time-and-materials billing) charges tax on the materials, not the labour (IB 4); the code's labour-and-materials-together contract is the general case. Earliest date: IB 4's revision of 2024-07-22.

summary: Transportation charges on exempt goods aren't taxed in Maine; on a sale of taxable and exempt goods, the charge is prorated.

citations.title: Maine Revenue Services, Instructional Bulletin No. 39, Sale Price Upon Which Tax is Based (last revised March 11, 2026)
citations.quote: When a sale has both taxable and exempt components (e.g., a restaurant buying both food and supplies), transportation charges may be partially exempt from tax if a proration is done.

citations.title: Maine Revenue Services, Instructional Bulletin No. 39 (last revised October 4, 2019)
citations.quote: When a sale has both taxable and exempt components (e.g., a restaurant buying both food and supplies), transportation charges may be partially exempt from tax if a proration is done.

notes: IB 39 states the exempt share by way of proration on mixed sales; no sentence says outright that delivery of wholly exempt goods is untaxed, though that follows (the charge is part of the sale price of an exempt sale). This holds however the goods travel, so it doesn't turn on the carrier facts in ME delivery.taxable_goods. Also in IB 39: if taxable items are 10% or less of the invoice, the whole transportation charge is deemed not taxable (de minimis), an exception to delivery.taxable_goods on mixed invoices. 2019-10-04 is the earliest edition read. Maine has no local sales tax.

summary: A separately stated delivery charge is excluded from Maine's taxable sale price when the goods ship by common or contract carrier or the U.S. mail; delivery in the seller's own vehicle is taxable.

Delivered in the seller's own vehicle

notes: How the goods travel is not carried by the code. Earliest date: conservative; § 1752(14) was last amended by laws of 2023, and the text read is current.
